The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. SPECIES sheet for a creature built from a shared body-plan kit: ROOTCRAWLER, a dog-sized beetle with dark green-bronze chitin, long mandibles and root fibres clinging to its legs, built on the shelled body plan. SCALE IS CRITICAL: it is only about 0.5 m tall at the shoulder and 1 m long, the size of a dog, its back no higher than the knee of the 1.8 m human figure, drawn small next to the figure with a thin dimension line labelled "0.5 m". On the plain grey background, no tunnel, no roots in the background. Its parts, as on the parts sheet: Rootcrawler shell, Rootcrawler mandible, Rootcrawler leg, Long whip antennae, Roots carried growth. It HAS a storm-touched variant, which must be drawn: small at the bottom right in side view, labelled "Stormcrawler", the same beetle with a dark storm-blue shell crackling with a faint electric charge. Keep the base body and parts from the attached kit sheets and the creature's design from the attached plate. Below: a row of four square colour mask swatches (main, secondary, accent, pattern). Show a storm-touched variant, small at the right in side view and labelled, only when the subject names one; otherwise draw no variant at all. Show only the parts this creature uses, and no description text. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Place it beside the side view, at TRUE scale to the stated size. Title at the top: "Rootcrawler".
